beginner.headline: Macron Warns of Intensifying Hybrid Attacks
beginner.brief: French President Emmanuel Macron says Russian 'hybrid attacks' are intensifying against Europe. He has asked his government to protect important places. These important places are critical infrastructure and defence industry sites. France was targeted by these hybrid attacks in the past few weeks. Other European leaders also warn that Russia may be preparing attacks. A 'hybrid attack' uses military force with non-military methods like cyberattacks. It can also include spreading misinformation.

intermediate.headline: Macron Warns of Intensifying Russian Hybrid Attacks in Europe
intermediate.brief: French President Emmanuel Macron has warned that Russia's hybrid attacks against Europe have grown more intense. He stated that France has been affected by these attacks in recent weeks. Macron explained that he had ordered a plan to secure essential infrastructure and defense sites. A growing number of European leaders believe Russia may be testing their commitment to supporting Ukraine. The French president recently discussed the security impact of conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine with party leaders. He mentioned remarks by Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk suggesting Russia was planning drone and missile strikes against countries on Nato's eastern flank. Macron stated that the intent behind these actions is to intimidate Europeans and break their efforts to support Ukraine. He stressed that France would not be intimidated because European security is at stake in Ukraine. Prime Minister Tusk said there was a "real risk" of such strikes on Nato territory, which Moscow might claim were "accidental" to split the alliance. Last Sunday, a Russian drone hit a passenger train near the Ukraine-Poland border, shortly after European security officials had passed through. Hybrid warfare is a strategy combining military force with non-military methods like misinformation and economic pressure. Macron also addressed the energy situation, announcing a G7 meeting to discuss energy issues and raise the question of gas stocks.

advanced.headline: Macron Warns of Escalating Russian Hybrid Attacks in Europe
advanced.brief: French President Emmanuel Macron has warned that the threat of hybrid attacks by Russia against Europe and France has grown more acute. He revealed that France had recently experienced Russian hybrid attacks and affirmed that these would not go "without a response". Macron reiterated that the Russian hybrid threat against Europeans and France had notably escalated in recent weeks. He stated Russia's intent was to intimidate and disrupt efforts to support Ukraine, asserting that such actions would achieve the opposite effect. The president emphasized that Europe's security is intrinsically linked to the situation in Ukraine, thereby dismissing any notion of intimidation. He announced a directive for a plan to bolster the security of France's vital national assets and sensitive defence industry sites. This security measure specifically addresses threats from drone and cyberattacks, alongside other non-military methods. Hybrid warfare encompasses a broad strategy combining conventional military force with non-military tactics, including cyberattacks, misinformation, and economic pressure. Macron referenced a drone attack on Leipzig airport, reportedly blamed on Russia, and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk's concerns about potential Russian strikes against Nato's eastern flank. Tusk explicitly warned Polish MPs of a "real risk" of drone and missile strikes on Nato territory, which Moscow might falsely attribute to accidental causes to splinter the alliance. Furthermore, Macron announced France would convene a G7 meeting to address energy issues and discuss gas stocks with the European Commission. The G7 discussion aims to strengthen cooperation among member nations and prevent unnecessary tensions while also considering options for unlocking strategic energy reserves.
